text:
maria: Heads up — after the kernel swap to fused-attn-v2 on canary we saw p99 jump for short-context chat flows. Telemetry shows spikes around heavy KV misses.
ajay: saw that too. quick raw perf dump from the canary nodes:
```kernel=fused-attn-v2
avg_token_ms=2.1
p50=12ms
p95=48ms
p99=210ms
gpu_util=92%
kv_hit_rate=0.61
microbatch=4
queue_time_ms_p99=120ms
```
This is with microbatch=4 and kv_prefetch disabled.
ryan: p50 unchanged but p99 huge — classic queuing/tail build-up. If gpu_util is 92% we're at saturation and a few slow KV paths will blow out tails.
maria: we had turned kv_prefetch off to reduce memory pressure for the canary variant. Also we bumped microbatch from 2 -> 4 to try to improve throughput last week.
helen: two levers to try: reduce microbatch back to 2 (reduces queuing) or re-enable kv_prefetch (reduces miss tail). Also consider lowering our target admission util from 75% -> 65% so we keep headroom for spikes.
ajay: ran a quick local run with microbatch=2 + kv_prefetch=on: 
```kernel=fused-attn-v2
avg_token_ms=2.3
p95=40ms
p99=85ms
gpu_util=68%
kv_hit_rate=0.93
```
p99 is way better, throughput down but tails fixed.
maria: can we do a short canary rollback to fused-attn-v1 + microbatch=2 + kv_prefetch=on and compare? Need to know whether kernel change or batching/prefetch combo is main culprit. @infra-bot start canary?
infra-bot: canary deploy initiated: fused-attn-v1 -> start_ts=1802345801. routing=3% traffic. will collect p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, gpu_util every 30s.
ryan: also add a queue_time_ms metric per request and an admission_drop_count metric. Alert if p99>150ms for 5m and queue_time_ms_p95 > 80ms.
perf-bot: perf regression alert muted for canary window per standard process.
helen: on admission/load-shedding policies: propose soft-shed first — return a low-cost model variant (quantized or shorter context) if util>70% and seq_len>512. Hard reject only after fallback fails. This preserves user experience while protecting p99.
ajay: +1 to fallback-before-shed. Also consider increasing admission priority for cached KV hits: give requests with kv_hit=true a higher admission score so they get through during high util.
maria: that implies we need admission scoring to read kv_hit_hint from routing header. Can we do that quickly for canary? ops, @ryan any objections?
ryan: doable — we can add kv_hint to the routing weight computation, lightweight change. Will push a canary config flag.
helen: also request we document cost delta: rolling back kernel might increase token-cost by ~3% at microbatch=2. Smaller microbatch increases tokens/sec cost too. Need the numbers in the rollout plan.
maria: noted — I'll draft a short runbook: 1) canary v1+mb2+prefetch on; 2) compare p99 and throughput; 3) if p99 improved: keep fused-attn-v1 on prod while we iterate on fused-attn-v2 opt; 4) implement admission kv_hint + fallback flow; 5) run stress tests for 24h. Link to draft: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kernel-tail-workflow
ajay: after canary results we should also run synthetic tail-tests with injected KV latency to validate admission thresholds. I can add that to perf harness.
maria: thanks all. will post canary results in ~15m. :thumbsup:
